newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria rebels vow to fight on.
newsitem.headline: Algeria rebels vow to fight on.

text.p: The armed wing of Algeria's outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS), in a faxed statement on Tuesday, denied reports that large numbers of rebels were surrendering and vowed to pursue its armed struggle against the authorities.

The Islamic Salvation Army (AIS) said in a statement faxed to an international news agency in Paris the authorities had launched a media campaign to "mutilate the image of jihad (holy struggle) in Algeria".
It was not possible to authenticate the statement.

"This campaign also aims at deluding people that large numbers of 'gunmen' have surrendered to the forces of tyrants as a prelude to the total collapse of the 'armed groups'...(and aimed) at spreading the spirit of defeat in the hearts of the warriors and their supporters," said the statement, dated July 26.
"The AIS tells the tyrants in Algeria and everywhere that the holy warriors will remain faithful to the vow and will continue on the path (of jihad) and they will never surrender...
"The proof of that are the continued operations in the cities, villages and mountains and the killing of high-ranking members of the tyrant forces...," the group said.
The statement made no reference to a large scale operation by the security forces earlier this month in which up to 300 rebels died, according to Algerian newspapers.
News reports said these rebels were members of the Armed Islamic Group (GIA), often seen as the more ruthless rival of the AIS.
Nor did it mention massacres in which suspected rebels killed hundreds of civilians in recent weeks.
About 60,000 people have perished in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which the FIS had taken a huge lead.
